SpellcastingIntelligence is the casting stat. DC = 10 + half your Necromancer level (minimum 1) + Intelligence modifier: see Resolving Magic in Spellcasting in Arneyan for the full formula. Harmful or debuffing spells need a save, except Touch spells, which use a touch attack (see Spellcasting in Arneyan).
Undead MasteryControls undead up to a cap in undead points equal to your Necromancer level + your Intelligence modifier (+5 at 15th). A skeleton or zombie is 1 point, a wight 3, a skull lord 5 (see Soul Tax). Every undead you control counts towards this cap, however it came under your control. For a Necromancer, Undead Mastery and Soul Tax replace the duration and control limits of Animate Dead, Create Undead and Create Greater Undead. Bound undead pay Soul Tax.
AllegianceEvil once you keep undead raised (see Alignment).
KitAt character creation choose a Kit: Grave Warden, Soul Binder, Pale Master, or Wight Lord.
IdentityA master of death who raises and commands an army of the dead, pays its toll in magic and drifts towards undeath.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

Class Abilities

1st Level

  • Spell Use: Cast spells from the Necromancer spell list using standard slot progression. The save DC of your Necromancy spells is increased by 1 (Death Magic).

Raise the Dead

  • Your power over the dead: Animate Dead, Undead Mastery (see Core Chassis) and Soul Tax, below, work as one feature.
  • Animate Dead: Animate one corpse as a skeleton or zombie without expending a spell slot. Each free use is one corpse, uses the spell's action and range, and needs no onyx; Undead Mastery and Soul Tax replace the spell's duration and control limits.
  • Free daily uses scale with level: 1 use (levels 1-4), 2 uses (levels 5-9), 3 uses (levels 10-14), 4 uses (levels 15-19), 5 uses (levels 20+)
  • You begin play with one skeleton you have already raised.
  • Additional uses beyond the daily free limit require a 3rd level slot each (from 5th level); each raises one corpse
  • Animated undead count towards your Undead Mastery cap (a skeleton or zombie is 1 point) and persist until destroyed or dismissed
  • While you are Unconscious your undead finish their last order, then guard you. If you die, they break free at the next dawn; the GM determines their behaviour
  • At the table: your undead act together on your initiative and move as a group.
  • In a fight your undead act as squads: all your undead of one kind form one squad.
  • A squad makes one attack roll and deals one creature's damage, +1 for each other creature in it.
  • Each creature still takes damage, saves and is destroyed on its own.
  • Soul Tax: Each dawn, you maintain undead worth up to half your Undead Mastery cap in points (rounded up) for free.
  • Beyond that, each undead costs a spell slot of a level equal to its points or higher, or you lose control of it.
  • Upkeep may use no more than half your total spell slots (rounded up) each dawn.
  • Undead points by Level:
Undead LevelPoints (Soul Tax slot)Examples
1 or lower1skeleton, zombie, poltergeist, crawling claw
2 to 32ghoul, shadow, rusalka, allip
4 to 63ghast, wight, wraith, draugr, haunt, apparition, crypt thing
7 to 94spectre, banshee, mummy, revenant, bodak, ghost
10 or higher5skull lord
  • Undead whose slot cannot be paid immediately break free; the GM determines their behaviour

Command Undead

  • Command Undead: As an action, attempt to bring an uncontrolled undead within 30ft under your command, 1 + half your Necromancer level times per day.
  • Its Level cannot exceed your Necromancer level, and mindless undead save as normal.
  • Control lasts 1 hour per Necromancer level unless you pay Soul Tax for it at dawn.
  • The undead makes a Will save against your Class Save DC
  • Failed save: obeys your commands and counts towards your Undead Mastery cap
  • Successful save: no effect
  • A creature marked Solo cannot be commanded or bound.
  • A use may instead restore one undead you control to full HP.
  • Kit: gain the named abilities from your chosen Kit.

2nd Level

  • Lingering Death: When a creature takes necrotic damage from your spell, one undead you control may at once move up to its speed towards it.

3rd Level

  • Undead Resilience: At the start of each encounter, gain temporary HP equal to the undead points you control, up to your Necromancer level.
  • Example: zombie (1 point) + ghoul (2 points) + wight (3 points) = 6 temporary HP
  • Temporary HP last until the end of the encounter

4th Level

  • Bone Shield: Once per round, out of turn, when an attack hits you while one of your undead is within 5ft of you, the undead takes the hit instead.

5th Level

  • Deathsense: Always aware of undead and dying creatures within 60ft, even through walls.
  • Know the presence, number, and approximate Level of all undead within range
  • Know when any creature within range drops to 0 HP or below
  • Cannot be surprised by undead

6th Level

  • Necrotic Aura: Always active while you have undead under your control within 30ft.
  • Controlled undead gain +1 damage per hit and +2 HP per Necromancer level
  • Once per encounter, one creature has Disadvantage on its save against a Necromancy spell you cast

8th Level

  • Death's Grasp: Once per day, if reduced to 0 HP or below while you have at least one undead under your control within 30ft, choose one of them: it is destroyed and you stand at 1 HP.

10th Level

  • Undying Legion: Once per day, as an action, every undead you controlled that was destroyed this encounter rises again with half its HP.
  • Undead you control gain immunity to turning
  • Undead you control cannot be commanded by Necromancers or Clerics of lower level than you
  • Renown: Name: your deeds are known. Title: A dreaded name of your choosing. Grave-diggers and body-sellers deal with you quietly: remains and costly grave components cost you half. Your first follower, a living servant, joins you.

13th Level

  • Deathless Labour: In downtime your undead dig, haul, build, farm and guard at the pace of workers who never tire. A project with undead labour takes half the time.

15th Level

  • Death's Embrace: The line between you and death has blurred permanently.
  • Gain a permanent +1 to Intelligence. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation)
  • Immune to instant-death effects, as Death Ward, and to energy drain
  • Cause Wounds spells heal you as they heal an undead. No other necrotic effect heals you
  • You no longer age and cannot die of old age
  • Undead Mastery improves: Your Undead Mastery cap rises by 5 points.
  • Command Undead improves: An undead of Level 5 or lower gets no save against your Command Undead.
  • Renown: Holding: you may found a crypt as your Holding (see Your Holding (15th) in Keeps & Kingdoms).

17th Level

  • Call the Departed: Once a week, speak for 10 minutes with the spirit of anyone whose name and face you know, wherever they died.

20th Level

  • Lichdom: The secret of lichdom is yours (see Lichdom, below).
  • Becoming a lich still costs the phylactery, the poison and the ritual, and stays your choice.
  • A Necromancer who refuses lichdom gains instead one more free use of Animate Dead a day and Undead Mastery +5.
  • Renown: Necropolis: You may found a necropolis (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 skeletons or zombies rise from its dead to serve you, counting towards your Undead Mastery cap. While you hold it, those undead pay no Soul Tax.

Kits

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Necromancer folder. Drag one onto your character.

Choose one Kit at character creation.

  • Kits define your approach to the death arts: not what power you have, but how you use it and what it says about you.
  • Each kit reshapes how you raise and use the dead (Raise the Dead), and improves at 9th level.
  • Raising the dead is a profane act: one raising is a stain, but keeping undead raised drifts your Allegiance towards Evil (see Alignment in Arneyan in Book II).
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.

  • Bonus Spells: High Intelligence grants bonus spell slots:
  • Intelligence 13-15: one extra 1st level slot

Intelligence 18+: one extra 3rd level slot (the bonuses are cumulative, and each arrives only once your table gives you slots of that level)

  • Preparation: Each morning prepare spells equal to your level plus Intelligence modifier. Spend a slot of the appropriate level to cast any prepared spell.

Class-Only Spells

Disrupt Undead (Cantrip; Necromancy; V, S): Range 30ft; one undead takes 1d6 radiant damage (+1 die at 5th, 11th and 17th level); Will negates.

Touch of Fatigue (Cantrip; Necromancy; V, S, M): Touch; one creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll or attribute check before the end of its next turn (touch attack).

Cause Fear (1st; Illusion; V, S): Range 30ft; one creature of Level 4 or lower is Frightened for 1d4 rounds; Will negates.

Cause Light Wounds (1st; Necromancy; V, S): Touch; 1d8 necrotic damage plus 1 per level (max +5) (touch attack).

Bind Undead (2nd; Necromancy; V, S, M): Range 30ft; one undead of Level up to your Necromancer level obeys you for 1 day per level; Will negates. It counts towards your Undead Mastery cap.

False Life (2nd; Necromancy; V, S, M): Self; gain 1d10 + your level temporary HP for 1 hour per level.

Ghoul Touch (2nd; Necromancy; V, S, M): Touch; one living creature is Paralysed for 1 round per three levels (minimum 1); Fortitude negates, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success (touch attack, then the save). While Paralysed it gives off a stench: any other living creature that starts its turn within 10ft makes a Fortitude save or is Sickened until it starts a turn outside the stench.

Gentle Repose (3rd; Necromancy; V, S, M): Touch; one corpse does not decay and cannot be raised as undead for 1 day per level.

Halt Undead (3rd; Necromancy; V, S, M): Range 60ft; up to 3 undead within 30ft of each other are Paralysed for 1 round per level; Will negates (mindless undead get no save). The effect on a creature ends if it is attacked.

Ray of Exhaustion (3rd; Necromancy; V, S, M): Range 60ft; one creature gains two levels of Exhaustion; Fortitude negates. This spell cannot take a creature above Exhaustion level 3. The levels recover as ordinary Exhaustion.

Contagion (3rd; Necromancy; V, S): Touch; one creature catches a disease of your choice (see Disease & Poison in The Arneyan Codex), with effects starting at once (touch attack); it makes the disease's save against your spell DC.

Feign Death (3rd; Necromancy; V, S): Touch; a willing creature appears dead to all senses and spells for 1 hour per level and takes half damage from physical attacks.

Animate Dead (Greater) (4th; Necromancy; V, S, M‡ (black onyx, as Animate Dead)): As Animate Dead, but you may raise any skeleton or zombie block of Level 5 or lower, or a ghoul or shadow. The same control limits apply.

Bestow Curse (Greater) (4th; Necromancy; V, S): As Bestow Curse, but it lasts until Remove Curse cast by a higher-level caster, or Wish, ends it.

Enervation (4th; Necromancy; V, S): Range 60ft; one creature gains 1d3 levels of Exhaustion; Fortitude negates. This spell cannot take a creature above Exhaustion level 4.

Bone Armour (4th; Necromancy; V, S, M): Self; fuse a shell of bone over yourself for 1 hour per level: +4 AC, which stacks with Mage Armour, and an attacker who hits you in melee takes 1d4 piercing damage.

Fear (Mass) (5th; Illusion; V, S, M): 60ft cone; each creature is Terrified and must flee for 1 round per level; Will negates. Creatures of higher Level than yours are unaffected.

Symbol of Pain (5th; Necromancy; V, S, M): Touch a surface to inscribe a rune that lasts until triggered or for 10 minutes per level. When a creature you did not name reads or passes it, creatures within 60ft that can see it have Disadvantage on attack rolls and checks for 1 hour; Fortitude negates.

Harm (6th; Necromancy; V, S): as the reverse of Heal in Spellcasting in Arneyan (touch attack).

Control Undead (7th; Necromancy; V, S, M): Range 30ft; up to one undead per two levels, each of Level up to your level, obey you for 1 minute per level whoever made them; Will negates (mindless undead get no save). They count towards your Undead Mastery cap while controlled, then return to their old master or turn hostile.

Symbol of Death (7th; Necromancy; V, S, M‡ (as Symbol)): Touch a surface to inscribe a rune, triggered as Symbol of Pain. Living creatures within 60ft with up to 150 HP in total die, lowest HP first; each makes a Fortitude save to resist. One use.

Create Greater Undead (8th; Necromancy; V, S, M‡ (black onyx, 10 gp per Level of the undead)): Range 10ft; one corpse; cast at night only.

  • Raises one undead, its type set by your caster level: 15–16 a spectre, 17–18 a mummy, 19+ a ghost.
  • A creature marked Solo is never raised.
  • It uses that creature's stat block in Monsters & Treasure.
  • It obeys you permanently and counts towards your Undead Mastery cap.
  • Material: a black onyx worth 10 gp per Level of the undead, consumed.

Horrid Wilting (8th; Necromancy; V, S, M): Range 60ft; 30ft radius. Living creatures take 1d6 necrotic damage per level (max 20d6); Fortitude halves. Plants and water creatures take maximum damage.

Vile Blight (8th; Necromancy; V, S): 40ft cone; 1d6 necrotic damage per level (max 15d6), Fortitude halves; plants in the area die.

Lichdom

  • At 20th level the Necromancer has uncovered the secret of lichdom (from 15th, if they have studied the Black Tome, a Secret the GM places).
  • From 15th level you glimpse its outline, though you never become a lich by accident.
  • This is not a class feature: it is a door.
  • Whether you walk through it is entirely your choice, and the GM's to adjudicate.

The Requirements

  • The Phylactery: A phylactery must be crafted: a specially prepared object that will house your soul.
  • It must be of exceptional quality (worth no less than 500 gp) and personally inscribed with your true name in an ancient necromantic script.
  • The crafting requires 1 month of uninterrupted work and a successful Intelligence check (DC 20, Severe tier).
  • Failure means the object is destroyed and the process must begin again.
  • The Poison: A unique magical poison must be brewed: one that kills the body without destroying the soul.
  • The ingredients are rare and specific, typically including: the blood of a willing sacrifice (or your own blood at cost of 2d6 permanent Constitution loss), powdered bones of a creature that died of old age, and a soul fragment harvested via the Soul Bind spell.
  • Brewing requires 1 week and a successful Intelligence check (DC 20, Severe tier).
  • The Ritual: You must perform a 24-hour ritual at a site of significant necromantic power: a place of mass death, an ancient burial ground, or a location where the veil between life and death is thin.
  • At the ritual's climax, you consume the poison.
  • The soul binds to the phylactery.
  • The body dies and rises as a lich.

Mechanical Benefits

  • Undead type: immune to instant-death effects, poison, disease, exhaustion drain, paralysis, and mind-affecting spells
  • No longer needs to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe
  • Immunity to cold and lightning damage
  • Fear Aura: creatures within 30ft must make a Will save against your Class Save DC or be Frightened for 1 round on first sight each encounter
  • Touch Attack: the lich's touch deals 1d10+5 cold damage, and the target makes a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC or is Paralysed for 1d4 rounds
  • Phylactery: if the lich's body is destroyed, the soul retreats to the phylactery. A new body forms in 1d10 days within 10ft of the phylactery. True death is only possible if the phylactery is destroyed first
  • Undead Mastery cap increases by 5 points permanently
  • All Soul Tax costs are one slot level lower: 1-point undead are free to maintain

Mechanical Drawbacks

  • The lich radiates an aura of undeath: Detect Undead and Detect Evil reveal the lich automatically, even under magical disguise
  • Clerics and Paladins can attempt to turn the lich as if it were a Level 16 undead
  • The lich cannot enter consecrated ground without a successful Will save (DC 20, Severe tier) each round
  • Cure spells no longer heal the lich; Cause Wounds spells and Harm do
  • The lich no longer recovers HP from rest; damage can only be healed magically
  • Has no Constitution score; treat its modifier as +0 from now on. Its maximum HP does not change when it becomes a lich.
  • The phylactery is a vulnerability: if destroyed while the lich's body is alive, the lich immediately takes 10d10 damage (no save) as the soul bond fractures

Narrative Consequences

  • Lichdom is irreversible by any means short of a Wish spell and divine intervention, and even then only with the lich's willing cooperation
  • The lich's patron relationship changes fundamentally: powers of life may withdraw, powers of death may draw closer
  • Its Allegiance becomes Evil, as all undead are, and its Outlook drifts: the lich retains their personality and memories but emotional responses dull over decades. The GM may call for Will saves against increasingly callous decisions as time passes
  • The lich becomes a figure of dread in Arneyan, recognised by name, hunted by orders of Clerics and Paladins

The Phylactery

  • The phylactery is the lich's true self. The GM and player decide together what it looks like, where it is kept and how it is guarded. An enemy who learns the phylactery's location has leverage over one of the most powerful beings in Arneyan.
  • Destroying the phylactery takes 40 damage (AC 20, resistance to all damage except radiant, immune to the lich's own spells)
  • If the phylactery is destroyed while the lich lives, it has days equal to its Intelligence score to make a new one (1 week of work, same cost and check) before its soul unravels, losing 1d6 Intelligence a day
  • Upkeep: Once a year the lich feeds its phylactery one soul: a creature of Level 5 or more that it killed and caught with Soul Bind, released in a 1-hour rite at the phylactery.
  • For each year it misses, the phylactery starves, and a destroyed body reforms in 1d10 weeks instead of days; after 3 missed years it goes dark, and the next destruction of the body is true death.
  • One soul for each missed year restores it.
  • Every soul fed is one the Raven Queen is owed.
